instruction: I am compiling a concise historical inventory of genomic companion-diagnostic eligibility for protein kinase inhibitors with an ATC code beginning L01E whose first FDA drug approval occurred in 2023. Use approval and classification information available through 9 September 2026. Include a drug only if an FDA-approved companion diagnostic covered its initial indication on the date of that first drug approval. For each qualifying drug–gene pairing, report the approved ingredient form, preserving salts and hydrates; the gene; the source-stated reference transcript for individually enumerated amino-acid substitutions; the complete enumerated substitution set; and any additional eligible open-ended alteration class names. Combine eligible alterations across diagnostics covering the same initial indication on that date. Use original drug labeling, including corrections effective for the original approval, and the applicable historical device approval or supplement's indication-specific biomarker definition. This inventory requests the discrete classification in that definition: complete named substitutions and additional specific class names, with the cited definition supplying their biological qualifications. It does not request a freeform reconstruction of every prescribing requirement, specimen requirement, assay-performance parameter, or functional test for hypothetical variants. For additional classes, report the specific eligible class names rather than broad assay variant-type headings when a more specific class is defined; leave subordinate inclusions and examples in the cited definition rather than making them separate classes or enumerating an open-ended variant universe. Do not substitute whole-panel coverage, molecular drug targets, biomarkers governing prior therapies, later indications, or general assay detection claims for drug-specific companion eligibility. Establish the complete approval/classification scope, use each first approval date and initial indication to select the historical diagnostic record, and follow that record to its detailed genomic definition. Legal APIs, bulk downloads, and source-discovered batches are valid retrieval methods.
output_format: Return a pipe-separated table with header drug|biomarker|reference_transcript|named_substitutions|additional_classes. Use one row per drug–gene pairing, sorted by drug and then gene. Use standard gene symbols. Give transcript accessions exactly as stated, including a version only if the definition supplies one; use NONE when no individually named substitutions are enumerated. Write substitutions in bare one-letter amino-acid notation without a p. prefix, as an unordered comma-, semicolon-, or whitespace-separated list; use NONE when there are none. For additional_classes, use the source's full class names in singular form, omitting introductory 'any' and generic suffixes 'mutation', 'alteration', or 'event'; replace internal spaces and hyphens with underscores so each class is one list token. Separate class tokens with commas, semicolons, or whitespace, in any order; use NONE when there are no additional classes. Keep cells on one line and put citations after the table, identifying the historical diagnostic definition and original approval/indication evidence. The cited definitions retain all their qualifications; the table is a classification inventory, not a standalone prescribing rule.
